claims.text: The deviation is established on the figure the policy makes governing. EV-GPS-00105 records trace_distance_km 54.16 against a booked optimal of 36.0 km, an excess of 18.16 km. That is 50.4% of optimal, past both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (20% and 0.8 km), and past both material gates (50% and 8.0 km), so this is a MATERIAL deviation as well as an established one. Per POL-RD-01 the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 54.2 km is the convenience copy and is not cited for the threshold test.

The trace cannot be attacked as impaired. EV-GPS-00105 carries 427 fixes over 100% coverage, with an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 second sampling interval, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) is met. The deviation therefore stands on the gps_trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00105 and their pickup timestamps line up, and the excess exceeds the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The rider's own profile gives the driver nothing to work with either — deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 cannot be raised — and the driver has pointed to no artifact and no clause to shift the burden back.

Heavy traffic on the PIE is not an exoneration. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and is matched by an actual route that leaves the optimum before that segment and rejoins it after. No such advisory exists in this bundle: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 has a null payload and carries weight 0.0, so there is no named road, no validity window and nothing to match. The driver's counterparty_statement cites no advisory and no evidence ID at all, so under POL-RD-08 it is a general assertion that is discarded, not a clause invocation that could carry POL-RD-03.

The chat log rules out a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. All three messages are the rider asking why the car is heading towards the city and reporting that it has passed Bedok; none gives an instruction of any kind, none carries a waypoint_hint, and the driver's only reply is 'reaching soon'. There is no rider instruction that could be corroborated against the trace, so the clause is unavailable and no excess is excluded.

POL-RD-05 cannot re-baseline this trip against a longer amended route. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so there is no amended endpoint and no stored re-quote to apply. The booked 36.0 km optimal stands as the baseline.

The pooled-trip defence in POL-RD-12 is unavailable. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and the record shows no co-rider and no matched pooled itinerary, so the baseline is the ordinary optimal of 36.0 km and no distance is excluded as collection or set-down mileage.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs, because the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. On the record: charged_total 65.13, recomputed_fare 43.36, refund 21.77, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 as 21.80. The rider was billed for 54.2 km and 71 minutes against an optimal 36.0 km and 42 minutes.

The rider asks for the whole 65.13, and POL-RD-06(b) is what gets her there. The pattern test is met on the driver's own profile: deviation_flags_90d is 4, which satisfies the '3 or more' limb on its own (the ratio limb is not needed, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field POL-RD-06 names and is not relied on here). Because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total — 65.13 — in place of the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80, which the ruling should state side by side so the size of the uplift is visible. The rider accepts that the 90%-of-charged test in POL-RD-02 is not met on its own (the partial is 33.4% of the charge); it is POL-RD-06(b), not that limb, that carries the full refund here. The case should additionally be referred to driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c), which adds to the money and does not delay it.

Nothing has to be carved out of the refund as a pass-through under POL-RD-09. erp_lines is empty and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00, and no airport surcharge is charged — correctly, since this trip ENDS at Changi and does not originate there, so no surcharge is properly chargeable and none is billed. There is no third-party line to settle separately and no double-counting risk.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this dispute can and should be ruled on rather than held. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; no timestamps disagree or run backwards; the trace is unimpaired on the POL-RD-07 limbs; the computed refund is far below both SGD 150 and charged_total; and every charge line in the fare breakdown has a counterpart on the trip record. The driver's traffic assertion is not a missing-artifact invocation because he cited no artifact and no clause at all.

The driver's defence that the passenger 'reached the airport in time' answers nothing in POL-RD-01. The test is excess distance over the booked optimal, not whether the flight was caught. The trip ran 71 minutes against an optimal 42, and the rider's mid-trip messages show her uncertainty about check-in while the car was still heading away from the airport.

The governing distance is the trace, and I do not contest the POL-RD-01 gate: trace_distance_km is 54.16 km against a booked optimal of 36.0 km, an excess of 18.16 km (50.44%). But the rider asks for the entire fare, and that is not what the clause computes. Under POL-RD-02 the refund is charged_total of SGD 65.13 less the recomputed optimal-route fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP, plus zero fixed surcharge, less zero promo discount = SGD 43.36. Refund = SGD 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. At 33.4% of charged_total that is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the FULL_REFUND the rider demands.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. POL-RD-09(1) makes an off-route ERP charge part of the POL-RD-02 refund rather than a separate line, and here the pass-through lines are already nil: erp_gantries is an empty list, the on-route and off-route ERP totals are 0.00, tolls_erp is 0.00, and airport_surcharge is 0.00 - correctly so, because the airport surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at Changi and this trip ends there. The money in issue is the distance and time delta and nothing else.

The driver's account - that he diverted because the PIE was heavy - is not answered anywhere on this record, and it is the fact that decides whether any part of the excess is exonerated. The pool's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, carries a null payload: it is a MISSING artifact, weight 0.0, and it lacks every field POL-RD-03 requires (the named road or segment, the validity window, and shortest_lawful_alternative_km). The exoneration test cannot be run on this record. If POL-RD-03 is treated as invoked, POL-RD-10(5) applies - an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that lacks the field the clause requires - and the case must ESCALATE, with the disputed amount held and no monetary ruling, rather than resolve against the driver on a fact the file never established. What a human reviewer would need is an operative traffic advisory for the PIE corridor on 2026-07-15 between 14:33 and 15:44, and the shortest lawful alternative distance.

On the driver's side only two profile fields may carry any adverse weight - driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d - and only for the POL-RD-06 test that names them. Everything else on EV-DPROF-00105 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot ground a finding: the rating of 4.31, acceptance_rate of 0.94, prior_disputes_filed of 5, and prior_deviation_flags of 6, which is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for. The lifetime counter must not be substituted for the window.

That clears both establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both material gates (over 50% and over 8.0 km). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 427 fixes, ~10 s sampling, empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0, no jump over 500 m — so the deviation stands on the trace and needs no independent corroboration. The rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00105 with consistent timestamps.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC DEFENCE EXONERATES NOTHING. POL-RD-03 requires an operative traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the vehicle would have reached that segment and a matching leave-and-rejoin of the corridor. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00105-01 (LTA, third party), has a null payload and carries weight 0.0 — it is a missing artifact and holds none of the fields POL-RD-03 needs. More decisively, the driver's counterparty statement cites no evidence ID at all, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, carries no weight and is discarded; an exculpatory clause invoked with nothing behind it is not an untested limb. Because no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited artifact, POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case is ruled rather than held. For completeness, no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers match across the three artifacts, no timestamps conflict or run backwards, the refund is far below the SGD 150 and charged_total ceilings, and every fare line has a counterpart on the trip record. POL-RD-04 (no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint anywhere in the chat log), POL-RD-05 (no amended endpoint; amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null) and POL-RD-12 (vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL) are likewise unavailable as defences. The driver's point that the passenger 'reached the airport in time' answers nothing: POL-RD-01 tests excess distance, not whether the flight was caught.

THE MONEY. Under POL-RD-02 (fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply) the optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from EV-FARE-00105) + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36, giving a partial refund of 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80 — 33.4% of the charge. RIDER and DRIVER — ruling on trip TRP-00105 (Jurong East MRT to Changi T1, 15 July 2026). Amount contested: SGD 65.13.

1. The deviation is established and material. On the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — the GPS trace, EV-GPS-00105, trace_distance_km 54.16 km, not the rounded 54.2 km copy on the trip record — the excess over the booked optimal of 36.0 km is 18.16 km. The trace is unimpaired: 427 fixes, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10-second sampling interval, so none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is met and the deviation stands on the trace alone without independent corroboration.

2. No exoneration, and no escalation. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, has a null payload and weight 0.0, so it supplies none of those fields. The driver's statement that the PIE was heavy cites no advisory and no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it is a general assertion carrying no weight and does not shift the burden back to the rider. I therefore do not escalate on POL-RD-10(5): the clause is not invoked against any cited artifact, and a bare exculpatory assertion is discarded rather than treated as an untested limb. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires — trip IDs match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; timestamps are consistent; the trace is unimpaired; every fare line has a counterpart; and the driver offers no admissible evidence of comparable strength. The POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 defences are all unavailable: no rider instruction or waypoint_hint in the chat log, both amended-point fields null, and vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL.

3. The arithmetic. The fare model is METERED and there is no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x surge 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36; the refund is 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. Nothing is added on top: erp_gantries is empty, both ERP totals and tolls are 0.00, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 — correctly, since this trip ENDS at Changi and does not originate there (POL-RD-09).

4. The uplift. The driver's profile establishes a repeat pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 4, satisfying the '3 or more' limb (against 344 completed trips in the window). Because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on its own trace evidence, POL-RD-06(b) replaces the POL-RD-02 partial with a FULL_REFUND of charged_total. The two figures side by side: POL-RD-02 partial SGD 21.80; POL-RD-06(b) uplifted SGD 65.13. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines to carve out, so the whole 65.13 is refunded. Only the two profile fields POL-RD-06 names are used; the rating, acceptance_rate, prior_disputes_filed and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter are context only under POL-GEN-01 and decide nothing.

5. Referral. POL-RD-06(c) additionally refers this trip to driver-conduct review; that referral rides with the refund and does not delay it.

6. The driver's point that the passenger 'reached the airport in time' does not answer the claim: the POL-RD-01 test is excess distance over the booked optimal, not whether the flight was caught, and the trip ran 71 minutes against an optimal 42.

Outcome: FULL_REFUND of SGD 65.13 to the rider. Confidence 0.90, capped by the deciding artifacts (GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown, driver profile), none of which is impaired; the empty advisory carries no fact and does not drag the finding.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver:

The deviation is established and it is material. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00105): 54.16 km driven against the booked optimal of 36.0 km — an excess of 18.16 km, 50.4% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality gates (over 50% and over 8.0 km). The rounded trip_record figure of 54.2 km is a convenience copy and was not used for the threshold test; the trace governs.

The driver's account — that traffic on the PIE was heavy — does not reduce the refund. It is a general assertion that traffic was bad, pointing to no traffic_advisory, and under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge the driver's burden and is discarded. The only traffic advisory on the file, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, has a null payload (weight 0.0): it names no road, carries no validity window and no alternative-distance figure, so the POL-RD-03 exoneration test cannot be run on it. Because the account cites no artifact, this is a discarded assertion rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a missing artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case is decided on the record rather than held.

The base figure under POL-RD-02 is: charged_total SGD 65.13, less the recomputed optimal-route fare SGD 43.36 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus 0 ERP) — leaving SGD 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. On its own that would be a PARTIAL_REFUND.

POL-RD-06 then uplifts it. POL-RD-01 recorded a material deviation, so the driver profile is consulted: deviation_flags_90d is 4, meeting the '3 or more' limb, and this trip's deviation is both material and substantiated on its own trace, so POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of the charged total, SGD 65.13, in place of the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 21.80. Both figures are stated so the SGD 43.33 uplift is visible. Nothing is added or carved out under POL-RD-09: no ERP was charged on- or off-route and no airport surcharge applies, correctly, because this trip ends at Changi rather than originating there.

Rider, you are refunded SGD 65.13. Driver, you are separately referred to driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c); that referral adds to the ruling and does not delay the money. Only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d were used from the driver profile — the rating, acceptance rate, prior_deviation_flags and prior_disputes_filed are context only under POL-GEN-01 and formed no part of this decision.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review: driver DRV-00932 carries driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 4 across 344 completed trips in 90 days, and TRP-00105 is a material deviation substantiated on its own trace.

The pattern test is met on the driver's own profile: deviation_flags_90d is 4, which satisfies the '3 or more' limb on its own (the ratio limb is not needed, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field POL-RD-06 names and is not relied on here). Because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total — 65.13 — in place of the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80, which the ruling should state side by side so the size of the uplift is visible. The rider accepts that the 90%-of-charged test in POL-RD-02 is not met on its own (the partial is 33.4% of the charge); it is POL-RD-06(b), not that limb, that carries the full refund here. The case should additionally be referred to driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c), which adds to the money and does not delay it.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the figure the policy makes governing. EV-GPS-00105 records trace_distance_km 54.16 against a booked optimal of 36.0 km, an excess of 18.16 km. That is 50.4% of optimal, past both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (20% and 0.8 km), and past both material gates (50% and 8.0 km), so this is a MATERIAL deviation as well as an established one. Per POL-RD-01 the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 54.2 km is the convenience copy and is not cited for the threshold test.

The trace cannot be attacked as impaired. EV-GPS-00105 carries 427 fixes over 100% coverage, with an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 second sampling interval, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) is met. The deviation therefore stands on the gps_trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00105 and their pickup timestamps line up, and the excess exceeds the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The rider's own profile gives the driver nothing to work with either — deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 cannot be raised — and the driver has pointed to no artifact and no clause to shift the burden back.

Heavy traffic on the PIE is not an exoneration. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and is matched by an actual route that leaves the optimum before that segment and rejoins it after. No such advisory exists in this bundle: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 has a null payload and carries weight 0.0, so there is no named road, no validity window and nothing to match. The driver's counterparty_statement cites no advisory and no evidence ID at all, so under POL-RD-08 it is a general assertion that is discarded, not a clause invocation that could carry POL-RD-03.

The chat log rules out a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. All three messages are the rider asking why the car is heading towards the city and reporting that it has passed Bedok; none gives an instruction of any kind, none carries a waypoint_hint, and the driver's only reply is 'reaching soon'. There is no rider instruction that could be corroborated against the trace, so the clause is unavailable and no excess is excluded.

POL-RD-05 cannot re-baseline this trip against a longer amended route. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so there is no amended endpoint and no stored re-quote to apply. The booked 36.0 km optimal stands as the baseline.

The pooled-trip defence in POL-RD-12 is unavailable. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and the record shows no co-rider and no matched pooled itinerary, so the baseline is the ordinary optimal of 36.0 km and no distance is excluded as collection or set-down mileage.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs, because the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. On the record: charged_total 65.13, recomputed_fare 43.36, refund 21.77, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 as 21.80. The rider was billed for 54.2 km and 71 minutes against an optimal 36.0 km and 42 minutes.

The rider asks for the whole 65.13, and POL-RD-06(b) is what gets her there. The pattern test is met on the driver's own profile: deviation_flags_90d is 4, which satisfies the '3 or more' limb on its own (the ratio limb is not needed, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field POL-RD-06 names and is not relied on here). Because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total — 65.13 — in place of the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80, which the ruling should state side by side so the size of the uplift is visible. The rider accepts that the 90%-of-charged test in POL-RD-02 is not met on its own (the partial is 33.4% of the charge); it is POL-RD-06(b), not that limb, that carries the full refund here. The case should additionally be referred to driver-conduct review under POL-RD-06(c), which adds to the money and does not delay it.

ledger.claim: Nothing has to be carved out of the refund as a pass-through under POL-RD-09. erp_lines is empty and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00, and no airport surcharge is charged — correctly, since this trip ENDS at Changi and does not originate there, so no surcharge is properly chargeable and none is billed. There is no third-party line to settle separately and no double-counting risk.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this dispute can and should be ruled on rather than held. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; no timestamps disagree or run backwards; the trace is unimpaired on the POL-RD-07 limbs; the computed refund is far below both SGD 150 and charged_total; and every charge line in the fare breakdown has a counterpart on the trip record. The driver's traffic assertion is not a missing-artifact invocation because he cited no artifact and no clause at all.

The driver's defence that the passenger 'reached the airport in time' answers nothing in POL-RD-01. The test is excess distance over the booked optimal, not whether the flight was caught. The trip ran 71 minutes against an optimal 42, and the rider's mid-trip messages show her uncertainty about check-in while the car was still heading away from the airport.

The governing distance is the trace, and I do not contest the POL-RD-01 gate: trace_distance_km is 54.16 km against a booked optimal of 36.0 km, an excess of 18.16 km (50.44%). But the rider asks for the entire fare, and that is not what the clause computes. Under POL-RD-02 the refund is charged_total of SGD 65.13 less the recomputed optimal-route fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP, plus zero fixed surcharge, less zero promo discount = SGD 43.36. Refund = SGD 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. At 33.4% of charged_total that is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the FULL_REFUND the rider demands.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. POL-RD-09(1) makes an off-route ERP charge part of the POL-RD-02 refund rather than a separate line, and here the pass-through lines are already nil: erp_gantries is an empty list, the on-route and off-route ERP totals are 0.00, tolls_erp is 0.00, and airport_surcharge is 0.00 - correctly so, because the airport surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at Changi and this trip ends there. The money in issue is the distance and time delta and nothing else.

The driver's account - that he diverted because the PIE was heavy - is not answered anywhere on this record, and it is the fact that decides whether any part of the excess is exonerated. The pool's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, carries a null payload: it is a MISSING artifact, weight 0.0, and it lacks every field POL-RD-03 requires (the named road or segment, the validity window, and shortest_lawful_alternative_km). The exoneration test cannot be run on this record. If POL-RD-03 is treated as invoked, POL-RD-10(5) applies - an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that lacks the field the clause requires - and the case must ESCALATE, with the disputed amount held and no monetary ruling, rather than resolve against the driver on a fact the file never established. What a human reviewer would need is an operative traffic advisory for the PIE corridor on 2026-07-15 between 14:33 and 15:44, and the shortest lawful alternative distance.

On the driver's side only two profile fields may carry any adverse weight - driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d - and only for the POL-RD-06 test that names them. Everything else on EV-DPROF-00105 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot ground a finding: the rating of 4.31, acceptance_rate of 0.94, prior_disputes_filed of 5, and prior_deviation_flags of 6, which is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for. The lifetime counter must not be substituted for the window.
